utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Eli, I’m just getting back from errands—have you heard any new updates about the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: No new updates on my end yet, Ira. I’d check the bulletin or ring the organizer to get the latest plan.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Got it — I’ll check the bulletin when I’m back inside, and maybe give the organizer a quick call too.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Leo, give me the quick version—what do you need me to bring for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Just bring a screwdriver set, some work gloves, and any spare tape or screws you’ve got.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it — screwdriver set, work gloves, and any spare tape or screws. I’ll bring what I have.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Just to confirm, the repair drive is still happening, right?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Yes, it’s still happening, as far as I know. I just want to double-check the timing and where people are supposed to drop things off so we don’t end up with confusion.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Got it — can you confirm the drop-off time and location when you check? I just want to make sure we’re not telling people the wrong thing.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh right, the repair drive — I meant to bring something for it. If you still need a hand, I can swing by and help out.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: That’d be great, Oren—extra hands are always useful. If you’ve got any spare screws, tape, or extension cords, bring those along too.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: You got it — I’ll rummage around for screws, tape, and an extension cord before I come by. If I can’t find much, I’ll still bring my two hands and a good attitude.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before I help, can you confirm what needs repairing and when the drive is?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: I think it’s for small household repairs, but I’m a bit fuzzy on the exact list and date—let me double-check before I tell you wrong.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Noah—I’d rather wait for the confirmed list and date than plan around a guess. Just let me know once you’ve checked.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry I’m late—how’s the repair drive going?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: No worries — it’s going pretty well so far, and we’ve already got a few things lined up to fix. Want me to catch you up?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Yes, please—give me the quick version, and tell me where I can jump in.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Happy to help with the repair drive, Gus. What do you need me to bring or fix?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Thanks, Sam — could you bring your drill and a hammer? If you’re up for a fix, the loose porch rail could use a hand.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: You got it — I’ll bring my drill and hammer, and I can take a look at that loose porch rail too.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I can help track that—where’s the repair drive being held?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: It’s being held in the school gym, right after pickup on Friday. I’ll bring the sign-up sheet so we can keep the repairs moving.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Perfect, I’ll note the school gym after pickup on Friday, and I’ll look for your sign-up sheet so we can keep folks organized.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, the repair drive? I heard they’re hoping to get a decent turnout this weekend, so I’m planning to stop by and see what they need.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Nice, I’ll spread the word too and maybe bring a few neighbors along. The more hands we have, the better!

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be wonderful, Quinn — I’m sure they’ll appreciate the extra help. I’ll let folks know we’re trying to make it a big neighborhood turnout!

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: How's the repair drive going, Rey? Do you still need help with anything?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Thanks, Mina — I could still use a hand sorting the donated parts, if you’re free.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Sure — where do you want me to start sorting the donated parts?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Nell, I was just hearing folks are getting a repair drive going—do you know what the plan is so I can pass it along?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I only heard it second-hand, but it sounds like people are still sorting out the time and who’s bringing tools. I’d wait to pass along details until someone closer to the planning confirms it.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Got it, I’ll hold off on spreading anything until we hear from someone actually organizing it.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Uli, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive moving—do you have a sense of which items neighbors are most eager to fix first?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Mostly the lamps and small appliances, I think. People want the little things working again first.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That makes sense—lamps and small appliances are a great place to start. I’ll note those as the first focus and make sure we have enough table space and basic tools ready.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hey Eli, have you heard about the repair drive yet? I was just trying to find out what folks need fixed and who’s bringing tools.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I hadn’t heard the details yet, Tess, but I’d be glad to help if there’s a clear list. What time is it, and what tools are folks short on?

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: I’m still piecing it together, but I heard they’re aiming for Saturday morning at the community room, and folks are especially asking for screwdrivers, pliers, and a decent socket set.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry I’m late — what’s left to do for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: We still need to sort the tools, set up the donation table, and make one last sweep of the list. I’ll repeat the plan to everyone so we stay on track.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Got it — I can jump on sorting the tools or help set up the donation table. Just point me where you need me most.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I haven’t heard the details yet, but I’d like to help if I can. What’s needed for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thanks, Rey. We mostly need a few hands, some basic tools, and maybe lumber and paint if anyone can spare them.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can help with the hands, and I might be able to bring a few basic tools too. If you send the time and place, I’ll come by.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Opal, I’m a little slammed, but I caught something about the repair drive—what’s the quick version of what you need?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Quick version: I’m trying to pin down where the repair supplies are going and who’s covering each drop-off, so I need any locations or timing you’ve heard.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it — I don’t have the full list, but I heard the church basement is one stop Saturday morning. I’ll text you if I catch any other times.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Hana, I’m glad we’re doing the repair drive — want me to help organize who brings what?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Yes, that would help a lot, Jules — before we make the list, can we confirm which repairs we’re prioritizing and how many neighbors have signed up?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely — let’s first pin down the top repair needs, then I’ll check the signup count and match people to supplies from there.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right, the repair drive—sorry, I’ve been a bit scattered today. What still needs doing?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: No worries — we still need to sort the donations and check the tool table. If you can help with either, that’d be a big help.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Yeah, I can help — I’ll start sorting the donations. If you need me at the tool table after that, just wave me over.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Oh, right — how’s the repair drive going? I can spread the word while I’m out running errands.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: It’s going well so far — thanks, Ira. If you hear folks mention it, tell them I can lend a hand and a few tools too.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Will do, Gus — I’ll let folks know you’re willing to help and have tools to lend.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need me to bring or do?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Could you bring your drill and help sort the tools? That’d be a big help.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I’ll bring my drill and help sort the tools. What time should I come by?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I can help, but I’d want to know the exact time, where to drop things off, and who’s coordinating it. Logistics get messy fast if we don’t pin that down first.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Fair point — what time are we aiming for, where should people drop things off, and who’s coordinating the drive?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’d suggest Saturday from 10 to 2, with drop-off at the community room entrance, but we need one named coordinator on the flyer so people aren’t guessing.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Cleo, I’m helping spread the word about the repair drive—if you can swing by, I’d love to see you there!

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I can make it, Quinn — and I’ll bring what supplies I’ve got on hand.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: That’s fantastic, Cleo—thank you! I’ll let the others know you’re coming with supplies.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Oren, I’m trying to line up the repair drive around school pickup times—do you know what window works best for families?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, I think most folks are freer right after pickup, maybe around 3:30 to 5—though let me double-check with a couple parents before you set it in stone.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That’s helpful, thanks — after pickup sounds like the best window. Let me know what the other parents say, and I’ll plan around that.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell, I’m glad I caught you—I'm organizing the repair drive and wanted to see if you’d be willing to help spread the word on your end of the block.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Sure, I can spread the word around my end of the block. Just send me the details, and I’ll pass them along.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Wonderful, thank you, Nell. I’ll send you the time, location, and a short blurb today so it’s easy to share.
